item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is preferable because it preserves FilesService.Add unchanged, while A materially changes that lower-level API’s streaming, memory, and error behavior. B still violates the required reuse path and has weaker retry tests, so it needs revision before merge.","reasons":["B preserves Add’s existing implementation and behavior; A unconditionally buffers every custom multipart body with io.ReadAll, changing streaming characteristics, memory usage, read timing, and reader-error wrapping.","Both reuse internal/multipartbody.NewFile and correctly encode the field as \"file\" with the supplied filename.","Neither candidate follows the explicit requirement that Upload route through FilesService.Add. B duplicates Add’s request construction and response decoding; A calls a newly extracted private add method instead.","A has substantially better retry verification: it uploads from an os.File and checks filename and content on every attempt. B merely counts requests, so it would not detect an empty replayed body, and its test omits RetryAllMethods: true from the reported scenario and frozen contract contexted behavior expectations. Still, recorded gates mean this weakness is test quality rather than proof of runtime failure here."],"risks_a":["Changes Add despite the contract requiring its existing behavior to remain intact.","Forces arbitrary caller-built bodies into memory and may introduce a new failure point before request construction.","Upload bypasses Add, contrary to the required API routing, even though some implementation is shared privately instead."],"risks_b":["Duplicates Add’s option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error, creating maintenance drift and directly violating the required routing through Add.","Retry test does not verify multipart body replay and does not enable RetryAllMethods as in the reported use case.","Visible tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader errors, as explicitly requested."]}
